# Nestlé S.A. (NSRGY / NESN.SW) — Research Report

*Based solely on data provided (web-collected as of 2026-08-16). Not live data. Gaps and inconsistencies are flagged explicitly rather than resolved.*

## Fundamental
H1 2026 sales: CHF 43.1B, organic growth +3.6% (RIG +1.5%, pricing +2.1%); Q2 alone +3.7% (RIG +1.8%). Emerging markets ex-China grew +7.1% (RIG +3.9%) vs. developed markets +2.3% (RIG +0.6%) — developed growth is almost entirely price-driven. **Key ambiguity**: GAAP net profit fell 31.4% (CHF 5.1B→3.5B) while underlying net profit was CHF 5.7B (-2.4% reported, +3.4% constant-currency) — a ~CHF 2.2B gap with **no reconciling items disclosed**. No actual H1 margin figures exist; only guidance that FY margin will improve. FCF improved CHF 2.3B→3.4B. Cost program at CHF 1.7B of CHF 2B FY target. FY guidance: 3–4% organic growth, margin improvement, FCF >CHF 9B (implies ~CHF 5.6B+ needed in H2).

## Dividend Quality
16 consecutive years of increases, latest +4.09%. Payout ratio ~86.9% (vs. JNJ 46.19%) — high, and **it is not disclosed whether this is GAAP- or underlying-based, nor whether it reflects the 31.4% profit decline**. No FCF payout ratio is provided at all, despite being requested — a material gap for judging cash coverage. Annual payment cycle, subject to AGM approval each year (no history of rejection given). Swiss withholding tax 35% (treaty-reducible to 15%, not automatic) is a tax rather than sustainability factor.

## Valuation
Trailing P/E 28.53 vs. forward P/E 17.62–17.72 — a large, unexplained gap, plausibly (not confirmedly) linked to the depressed GAAP earnings. Forward P/E is +23.1% above CPG sector median (14.32) — the **one clean, single-source valuation signal** in the dataset, reading moderately expensive. Peer comparison is mixed-basis (Nestlé forward vs. Unilever 12.93 trailing, Danone 22.54 trailing) — Nestlé screens mid-pack. DCF: two sources disagree by >50% on fair value ($113.62 vs. $179.01) and don't agree on current price ($77.76 vs. $102, ~31% gap); both imply undervaluation (+46.1%/+43%) but cannot be verified as apples-to-apples. Market cap also diverges ~1.5x ($258.56B vs. $385B), unexplained. Currency mixing (CHF/USD/EUR, no FX given) undermines cross-source comparisons throughout.

## Technical
Price 79.06 (CHF). 5-day (72.04) and 50-day (71.85) MAs below price, flagged "buy"; 200-day (74.52) also below price but flagged "sell" — classification logic not explained. RSI(14) 50.83 — neutral. Support 78.99 (price is just 0.07 above it), resistance 81.65 (~3.3% away). Composite signal: 8 sell vs. 4 buy, despite individual short/medium MA readings being "buy" — an unresolved internal contradiction. A separate cited target ($87 from $71, +23%) appears USD-based and cannot be reconciled with the CHF-based levels above absent an FX rate.

## Industry
Largest global food/beverage company by revenue (~$89.88–92B, ~2% source spread, plausibly minor). Nearest comparable peer by revenue: Unilever (~$60B). Danone: $53B cap, €27.283B revenue (different currency, no FX to normalize). Other named peers (PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Mondelez, Mars) lack comparable figures, so "largest by revenue" is plausible but not exhaustively verified. Strategy: consolidation into four core categories (Coffee, Petcare, Nutrition, Food & Snacks); Blue Bottle Coffee sold to Centurium Capital (China PE), price undisclosed. Emerging threat: AI/platform-based premium nutrition startups cited at 12% share of an undefined "premium nutrition segment" — single unverified citation.

## News/Event
CEO Laurent Freixe removed after internal investigation; Chairman Paul Bulcke departed early — near-simultaneous, unusual, cause undisclosed. New CEO Philipp Navratil issued a 5-point turnaround plan. Restructuring: 16,000 jobs cut (12,000 white-collar, 4,000 manufacturing/supply chain); savings target raised CHF 3.13B→3.76B. The restructuring announcement (Oct 2025) precedes the profit decline (reported Jul 2026) — **temporal sequence confirmed, causation not established**. Blue Bottle sale consistent with portfolio-focus strategy but financial impact unknown (price undisclosed).

## Sentiment
Analyst consensus (5 institutions, ADR): 3 buy/1 hold/1 sell, "Buy" overall; average target $113.68, range $97.00–$127.40 (~31% spread — significant disagreement); implies +18.91% upside. Same source class reportedly rated "Hold" ~1 year earlier — shift unexplained (fundamentals vs. coverage-set change unknown). Currency mismatch (USD targets vs. CHF technical levels) prevents direct comparison to resistance/support levels.

## Bull Case
Underlying profit +3.4% (constant-currency) despite GAAP decline; emerging-market volume growth (RIG +3.9% ex-China) is genuine demand strength; FCF and cost program both ahead of/tracking well; savings target raised, not cut; new leadership acted decisively (5-point plan, category focus, Blue Bottle divestment); forward P/E discount to trailing may reflect market anticipating earnings normalization; both DCF models agree directionally on undervaluation (43–46%); short/medium MAs and neutral RSI show no breakdown; analyst sentiment improved to "Buy." Bull must concede: GAAP decline is real and unexplained; payout basis is unclear; DCF/market-cap figures are internally inconsistent; the technical *composite* is sell-dominant; currency mixing undercuts several cited percentages.

## Bear Case
GAAP net income — the number that accrues to shareholders — is down 31.4% with zero disclosed reconciling items; no H1 margin data exists to check management's improvement claim. Growth is largely price-driven, especially in developed markets (RIG +0.6%); China is entirely absent from the data, a meaningful blind spot. Payout ratio (86.9%) may understate true current coverage if computed pre-decline; no FCF payout ratio is available at all. Sector-relative forward P/E (+23.1% premium) is the one clean valuation datapoint and it reads expensive, not cheap; DCF "upside" is too internally inconsistent to rely on. Technical composite is sell-dominant with price sitting almost exactly at support. Simultaneous CEO/Chairman exit following an internal investigation is a governance red flag. Restructuring costs may be conflated with the earnings decline. The "Buy" sentiment consensus is recent, narrow, and dispersed (31% target range), following a "Hold" rating a year prior with no explanation.

## Synthesis
Bull and bear rely on the **same underlying facts**; they diverge on how to weight disclosure gaps, not on the numbers themselves. The single largest unresolved question — whether the 31.4% GAAP profit decline is one-off restructuring noise or structural deterioration — **cannot be answered from this data**, since no reconciling items are disclosed. Valuation is similarly unsettled: the only clean, single-source figure (sector-relative forward P/E) reads moderately expensive, while the DCF "undervaluation" case rests on two mutually inconsistent models with unreconciled currency/price bases and a ~1.5x market-cap discrepancy. The technical read is internally contradictory (sell-dominant composite vs. buy-flagged short/medium MAs). Other open questions — China's standalone performance, the payout ratio's earnings basis, the cause of the Hold→Buy sentiment shift, and whether restructuring costs explain the GAAP profit gap — would each materially change the conclusion if resolved, but none can be resolved with the data provided. On balance, this dataset supports flagging real strengths (cash flow, cost-program pace, emerging-market volumes) alongside real, unresolved risks (earnings-quality opacity, thin/uncertain dividend coverage, governance shock, mixed technical signals) — not a confident directional call.

It does not constitute investment advice, a recommendation to buy or sell any security, or a substitute for independent due diligence and professional financial advice.
